messages.subject: CmdStan's stan_csv_reader (which is in the Stan Library)
parts:
So, I hacked that together over a weekend years ago and it's terrible. Full on embarrassing that I did that type of terrible.

Can we redesign it so it's maintainable, robust, and isn't a tangled mess? Bob, I would feel much better if you were involved with design.

We don't need it in Stan anymore since the writer refactor happened and we can access output directly. We need to update tests so they don't depend on flat files within Stan. This should make Mike's work a lot easier to accomplish. (I think?)

Any takers?


Daniel

P.S. Krzysztof, if you wanted to deal with this one, it would help a lot. I'll keep thinking of other infrastructure places where we could use help.

Sure, I love this kind of thing. I see two issues for a general design.

1. Is it streaming or does it read the whole CSV file into
memory? That is, do we need something like a row callback
or a data structure representing the whole matrix of entries, or
both?

2. How do we deal with types? Each column should have a type
such as integer, string, or double (other types?).

- Bob

parts:
>
> 1. Is it streaming or does it read the whole CSV file into
> memory? That is, do we need something like a row callback
> or a data structure representing the whole matrix of entries, or
> both?
Reads everything in line by line, storing samples in an Eigen matrix.

> 2. How do we deal with types? Each column should have a type
> such as integer, string, or double (other types?).

Everything is read in as a string (if a name) or a double (if a value)
and then cast internally if necessary.

Honestly I could be talked into splitting the output files into a

model.meta (config + adaptation)
model.warmup.csv (warmup iterations)
mode.warmup.diag.csv (warmup iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)
model.samples.csv (sampling iterations)
mode.samples.diag.csv (sampling iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)

so that we could easily stream all of the output statistic calculations.

I would kill to have a generic way of stuffing all of those files into
some Stan output file type so that we have a single output file
but all of the info separated.

> - Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CmdStan's stan_csv_reader (which is in the Stan Library)
parts:
> On Mar 14, 2016, at 2:03 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>>
>> 1. Is it streaming or does it read the whole CSV file into
>> memory? That is, do we need something like a row callback
>> or a data structure representing the whole matrix of entries, or
>> both?
>
> Reads everything in line by line, storing samples in an Eigen matrix.

As long as they're not too big, this will work.

All of our output summaries are by column (I think), so this would
be good for numerical locality.

>> 2. How do we deal with types? Each column should have a type
>> such as integer, string, or double (other types?).
>
> Everything is read in as a string (if a name) or a double (if a value)
> and then cast internally if necessary.

Then we'd need to know which is which before parsing. Whereas
if we parse everything as a string, we can convert on reading. But
it'll take more storage, so I'd rather predeclare if we have to store
everything as a data structure. But then I'd suggest we need to do
it by column, because the types won't all be the same to store
in an Eigen matrix.

>
> Honestly I could be talked into splitting the output files into a
>
> model.meta (config + adaptation)
> model.warmup.csv (warmup iterations)
> mode.warmup.diag.csv (warmup iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)
> model.samples.csv (sampling iterations)
> mode.samples.diag.csv (sampling iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)
>
> so that we could easily stream all of the output statistic calculations.

I would very very strongly prefer that. Then there's going to
be duplication for multiple chains, so it will be a pain to organize.
The easiest thing to do would be to assign a directory for a run.

We don't manage multiple chains from within CmdStan, but maybe
we should? I think the x-platform multi-process issues are the killer.

> I would kill to have a generic way of stuffing all of those files into
> some Stan output file type so that we have a single output file
> but all of the info separated.

All else being equal, I'd prefer a generic format, like zip or gzipped tar,
so people can pull it out with usual desktop/unix tools.

Or we could do the whole thing with protocol buffers or something
like that, which require a bit more than desktop tools to unpack,
but could be much more concise if we work out the streaming details.

- Bob

On Mon, Mar 14, 2016 at 2:16 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

> On Mar 14, 2016, at 2:03 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:

>>

>> or a data structure representing the whole matrix of entries, or
>> both?
>
> Reads everything in line by line, storing samples in an Eigen matrix.

As long as they're not too big, this will work.

All of our output summaries are by column (I think), so this would
be good for numerical locality.

Just to be clear, that's our current behavior. We read everything into memory. There's no requirement that we need to do that.

It's definitely easier to reason about things when everything is in memory. If you think we can stream it and it'll be ok, we can do that instead.

>> 2.  How do we deal with types?  Each column should have a type
>> such as integer, string, or double (other types?).
>
> Everything is read in as a string (if a name) or a double (if a value)
> and then cast internally if necessary.

Then we'd need to know which is which before parsing.  Whereas
if we parse everything as a string, we can convert on reading.  But
it'll take more storage, so I'd rather predeclare if we have to store
everything as a data structure.  But then I'd suggest we need to do
it by column, because the types won't all be the same to store
in an Eigen matrix.
Within the non-commented lines, only the header contains strings. Everything else is numeric: either integer or floating point. Right now, we promote everything.

>
> Honestly I could be talked into splitting the output files into a
>
> model.meta (config + adaptation)
> model.warmup.csv (warmup iterations)
> mode.warmup.diag.csv (warmup iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)
> model.samples.csv (sampling iterations)
> mode.samples.diag.csv (sampling iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)
>
> so that we could easily stream all of the output statistic calculations.

I would very very strongly prefer that.  Then there's going to
be duplication for multiple chains, so it will be a pain to organize.
The easiest thing to do would be to assign a directory for a run.

We don't manage multiple chains from within CmdStan, but maybe
we should?  I think the x-platform multi-process issues are the killer.
We could proc it, I think. I don't think we can reasonably multi-thread.

> I would kill to have a generic way of stuffing all of those files into
> some Stan output file type so that we have a single output file
> but all of the info separated.

All else being equal, I'd prefer a generic format, like zip or gzipped tar,
so people can pull it out with usual desktop/unix tools.

Or we could do the whole thing with protocol buffers or something
like that, which require a bit more than desktop tools to unpack,
but could be much more concise if we work out the streaming details.

I don't know how many people actually look at the csvs by hand. Here's what I think the normal workflow is.

1. Write foo.stan; compile foo, run foo, output into ___
2a. From CmdStan: ./bin/stansummary ___
2b. From RStan: fit <- read_stan_csv(___)

As long as we are able to maintain that workflow, I think we can change it around. Perhaps we no longer call it "read_stan_csv()." Or perhaps we write a CmdStan utility that outputs just the csv, but I think that's not so ideal.

So there's a protobuf-based writer that allows this sort of thing (mixing all the info in identifiable form into a single broadly-readable file) on a separate repository at the moment:
https://github.com/sakrejda/protostan/blob/develop/src/protostan/interface_callbacks/writer/binary_proto_stream_writer.hpp

Note that a) I'm not claiming that this is better than a zipped directory for broad use/portability; and b) I'm not saying the _design_ is right, but I have the mechanics of using protobuf for this down. It would be pretty straightforward to do a similar format and then allow the user to run a reader over it to pull out specific pieces into .csv for command line usage or some sort of Eigen-compatible mmapable format.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CmdStan's stan_csv_reader (which is in the Stan Library)
parts:
I would much prefer to keep at least the sample info
in CSV format as it makes it super easy to use with
other packages (in my case, graphics libraries).
On Mar 15, 2016, at 2:05 PM, Allen B. Riddell <a...@ariddell.org> wrote:

On 03/14, Krzysztof Sakrejda wrote:
On Monday, March 14, 2016 at 2:03:12 PM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:

1.  Is it streaming or does it read the whole CSV file into
memory?  That is, do we need something like a row callback
or a data structure representing the whole matrix of entries, or
both?

Reads everything in line by line, storing samples in an Eigen matrix.

2.  How do we deal with types?  Each column should have a type
such as integer, string, or double (other types?).

Everything is read in as a string (if a name) or a double (if a value)
and then cast internally if necessary.

Honestly I could be talked into splitting the output files into a

model.meta (config + adaptation)
model.warmup.csv (warmup iterations)
mode.warmup.diag.csv (warmup iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)
model.samples.csv (sampling iterations)
mode.samples.diag.csv (sampling iterations but unconstrained and with gradients and momenta)

so that we could easily stream all of the output statistic calculations.

I would kill to have a generic way of stuffing all of those files into
some Stan output file type so that we have a single output file
but all of the info separated.

So there's a protobuf-based writer that allows this sort of thing (mixing all the info in identifiable form into  a single broadly-readable file) on a separate repository at the moment:
https://github.com/sakrejda/protostan/blob/develop/src/protostan/interface_callbacks/writer/binary_proto_stream_writer.hpp

Note that a) I'm not claiming that this is better than a zipped directory for broad use/portability; and b) I'm  not saying the _design_ is right, but I have the mechanics of using protobuf for this down.  It would be pretty straightforward to do a similar format and then allow the user to run a reader over it to pull out specific pieces into .csv for command line usage or some sort of Eigen-compatible mmapable format.


Another option would be to stream everything into file
``model.jsonlines`` where each line was a valid JSON object, see
http://jsonlines.org/

It's not necessarily a lot of extra work: we have to do the

parts:
I see two things that this is trying to do.

Specify what the output is supposed to be for Stan.
A very good thing to do.

Specify how the writers work at a low level to make
sure we can express all that output.

Make a concrete, cross-interface proposal for a serialized
form of all this data as multiple files per chain, multiple
chains per run.

Round-trip is definitely a desirable goal. We can do it
in RStan pretty easily, but not in CmdStan (again, I have
no clue about PyStan).
